title: Two clones or branches of a committed loop can give two issues one number; every move of that number then lands on both, and verify calls it clean
claim: Numbers are taken from the clone's own issues, so two clones that each file an issue take the same number; git merges the two files without a conflict because their slugs differ; list then shows two issues numbered 2, verify reports clean, and show and set reach only the first file, so the second issue cannot be addressed by number. Corrected by the sceptic: Add to the claim: every move of the number lands on both issues in the record (log.md), so list, resume and the done gate treat the second issue as moved too. verify reports the second file only as a header that disagrees with the log, and its advice would copy the wrong state into it. The cause also covers two branches of one checkout, not only separate clones.
evidence: Run on scratch repositories with Jarl a1132a8: materials/two-clones.md, section 'Two clones file one number'. The numbering reads this checkout and its worktrees only (jarl-lib.mjs:1562-1564), and new is refused in a linked worktree because "the number would be used twice" (jarl-lib.mjs:1523); nothing covers a separate clone. findIssue returns the first file with the number (jarl-lib.mjs:881).
proposal: verify and every command that reads issues refuse or report two issue files with one number, naming both; a design for ids that cannot collide across clones goes with the multi-driver part of research/2026-11-03-jarl-as-a-loop-tool.
verifier: fresh Opus sceptic, 2026-11-03, at JarlSkill a1132a8: stands-corrected. Reproduced, and nothing documented prevents it. The merge setup covers only log.md (union) and decisions.md (the jarl-decisions driver); .jarl/issues/ has no driver, and two files with different slugs never conflict, so the documented merge-driver flags change nothing. A clone gets no local driver configuration, and its first write adds none, because the setup runs only when .gitattributes is missing (jarl-lib.mjs:206-207). The numbering reads this checkout and its worktrees only (highestAcrossWorktrees, jarl-lib.mjs:1493-1500), and the guard on new refuses only a linked worktree (jarl-lib.mjs:1523). The docs say numbers never collide because the write lock hands them out (SKILL.md:99, references/jarl.md:45, references/repositories.md:40), and that lock lives in one checkout (references/record.md, The write lock). One correction makes it worse than written: set and every other move write the number into log.md, and the log is the record, so a move on 2 moves both issues numbered 2. After set 2 dropped, list shows both dropped while the second file still reads open. verify then reports the second file as disagreeing with the log and advises writing the log state into it, which would drop an issue nobody dropped. verify is clean only until the first move, and it never names the shared number. Two branches of one checkout that each file an issue end the same way.

title: A fresh clone of a committed loop with no issue yet cannot file one
claim: init --committed leaves .jarl/issues/ empty and git keeps no empty directory, so in a clone made before the first issue was committed new fails with a raw ENOENT on scandir of .jarl/issues instead of creating the directory.
evidence: Run on scratch repositories with Jarl a1132a8: materials/two-clones.md, section 'A fresh clone of a loop with no issue yet'. The number is taken with readdirSync on .jarl/issues with no existence check (jarl-lib.mjs:1562).
proposal: new creates .jarl/issues/ when it is missing in a loop whose goal exists; a test files the first issue in a fresh clone of a committed loop.
verifier: fresh Opus sceptic, 2026-11-03, at JarlSkill a1132a8: stands. Reproduced as written, for committed and permanent loops alike. init creates .jarl/issues/ (jarl-lib.mjs:1357) and writes no placeholder, so git ls-files lists no issues/. In the clone, verify, status, resume, list and next all pass, because the readers check that the directory exists (jarl-lib.mjs:1497, 5062); only new reads it with readdirSync and no check (jarl-lib.mjs:1562). init refuses in the clone because a live loop exists, so no command repairs it; ask and decide work. No doc names the case, and the clone test in tests/one-store.test.mjs files its issue before cloning. Medium is honest: new is blocked with a raw error, nothing is lost, and mkdir .jarl/issues gets past it once someone reads the message.
